To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ghana's NSI is in its infancy, with the majority of the actors being at an embryonic stage of development.

the Ghanaian NSI is characterized by a weak link between the government and the other three actors, and by the lack of a strong and effective link between the government, industry, and knowledge based institutions.
the DASI is a useful tool to measure the NSI of Ghana, but it needs to be improved.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of a systemic approach in order to map, measure, and manage the interactions of core actors in the Ghana NSI, in order to enable targeted policy for increased industrial development, economic performance and competitiveness.

(1) Mapping and measuring the NSI (2) Measuring and analysing innovation performance of the core actors in the Ghana NSI (3) Measuring the impact of policy on innovation performance of the actors (4) Identifying barriers to innovation performance of the Ghana NSI and the core actors (5) Developing policy recommendations for increasing competitiveness of the Ghana NSII.

the following: (i) mapping the Ghanaian NSI through a survey of four key actors (ii) measuring the performance of the Ghanaian NSIs through an index and (iii) managing the Ghanaian NSIS through targeted policy interventions to increase competitiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ghanaian NSI is not yet fully functional and that the NSI is still evolving.

, the Ghanaian National System of Innovation (NSI) is a weakly developed and underperforming system, with a high degree of fragmentation, a low level of interaction, and a lack of coordination between actors.

the NSI of Ghana has the potential to be a key enabler of industrial and economic development, but that this potential is being undermined by a range of barriers, which are both internal and external to the NSI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to map, measure, and thereby manage the Ghana NSI, and to do so in a way that has enabled us to make recommendations for the development of a targeted policy framework for innovation and development.
the Ghana NSI is characterised as a weakly integrated, weakly interactive and weakly dynamic system, with weak innovation capabilities.
we have been able to map and measure the Ghana NSI and thereby provide a basis for policy formulation to enhance the competitiveness of industry and the economy of the country as a whole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NSI is an effective tool in the formulation, implementation, and monitoring of policy.

the DASI approach is a useful tool for policy makers and development agencies to understand the innovation system of a country, to identify barriers to innovation and to target interventions for the purpose of increasing innovation and economic competitiveness.
a systemic approach is required to map, measure, and manage the interactions and barriers to innovation in the NSI.
